articles.title: Democrats seize control of Congress after flipping House and Senate
articles.summary: Democrats have regained control of Congress, winning back the U.S. House and Senate as Republican midterm losses mount. Coming into the night, Republicans held 53 of the Senate's 100 seats, compared with 45 held by Democrats. To wrest back control of the Senate, Democrats needed a net gain of at least four seats. Before the clock struck midnight on the East Coast, the Associated Press said the party would gain at least that amount. Democrats won a series of key Senate seats. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers in one of the most closely watched races. James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, becoming the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in the Lone Star State since 1988. Annie Andrews beat GOP Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina to flip a Senate seat. In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson defeated incumbent GOP Sen. Susan Collins, putting an end to her three-decade tenure. Sen. Jon Ossoff comfortably won reelection in Georgia. Other Senate seats to flip to the Democratic Party included Roy Cooper in North Carolina  and Sherrod Brown in Ohio. In the 435-seat House, the GOP held 218 seats, compared with 214 held by Democrats. To retake control of the House , Democrats needed a net gain of three seats — and the AP said early Wednesday that the party had exceeded that figure. There were also 36 gubernatorial races and numerous ballot measures to keep an eye on. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history, while Democrat Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor-elect. President Trump, whose approval ratings are at or near all-time lows, distanced himself from mounting Republican losses in a post on Truth Social on Tuesday night, "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" Trump wrote. "Thank you for your attention to this matter." articles.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins historic Senate race in Michigan
articles.summary: Former Wayne County and Detroit health director Abdul El-Sayed, a child of Egyptian immigrants who ran on a progressive platform and has withstood an unprecedented level of attack ads against him and a campaign where he was unfairly described as a "jihadist" and sympathizer to terrorism, made history Nov. 4 by winning Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat. Decision Desk HQ and Fox News called the race for El-Sayed by 2 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 4. He will become the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator when the next Congress takes office in January, having defeated Republican former U.S. Rep. Mike Rogers in a hard-fought race that saw incredible levels of outside spending and in-state intrigue right up to Election Day. El-Sayed, 42, of Ann Arbor, replaces Democratic U.S. Sen. Gary Peters who is stepping down after two six-year terms. With 70% of the vote tallied, El-Sayed led Rogers 52%-46% and hadn't trailed in the count all night. Rogers, a former FBI agent and staunch conservative making his second attempt in two years to win an open U.S. Senate seat in Michigan, was trying to overcome historical trends, political headwinds and the polls to become the first Republican to win a Senate seat in the state in 32 years. El-Sayed will join a new Democratic majority in the U.S. Senate, that party having already been projected to flip Republican-held seats in Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas. Michigan had been widely looked at as Republicans' best chance of flipping a Democratic-held seat. Democrats, riding a wave nationwide, also took control of the U.S. House headed into President Donald Trump's final two years in office. "You took a chance on the unlikeliest of candidates. This is all yours. Michigan, I cannot wait to serve you," El Sayed said in a speech to supporters in which he declared victory at about 1:30 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 4. "Thank your for your trust, and your belief and your kindness." "Michigan, we did it," he said. On Election Day, El-Sayed was greeted like a rockstar as he stopped at a polling place at his alma mater, the University of Michigan, being swarmed by students as he posed for photos on a day when the turnout of younger voters was expected to be a big factor in the outcome. Several students who met El-Sayed were moved to tears. A DJ played Michigan’s fight song as the crowd swelled outside a campus voting hub on South State Street. Pre-med students Anokhi Changra and Chloe Slawson, said they voted for the Democrat because they share his views on health care, the environment and abortion rights. “He’s just very morally and politically aligned with me,” Changra said. A conservative heckler who shouted at El-Sayed to denounce an Iranian military force or “any Islamic terrorist organization" was booed. But the Democrat's support stretched well beyond Ann Arbor. Leaving Livonia’s Webster Elementary School polling location about 1 p.m. Angela Fletcher-Cook, 47, of Livonia, said she was appalled by abuse directed at him during the campaign. "I think he’s going to be great for Michigan, that he really cares about us and wants the best,” she said. Breanna Wynn, a 27-year-old Detroiter, dropped off her ballot on election morning at the Northwest Activities Center in northwest Detroit, saying she was most excited to vote for El-Sayed as the candidate who she felt would fight most strongly against the Trump administration’s attempts to dismantle democracy, but added that all her votes up and down the ballot mattered to her greatly. “If you didn’t vote in the midterms, you didn’t vote,” she said. Rogers without question had enormous support as well. West Bloomfield resident Tammy Shammaz, 61, voted at her polling place at Covenant Baptist Church in the township shortly before noon. A longtime Republican, she said she was enthusiastically supporting Rogers as well as Republican U.S. Rep. John James in the governor's race. "We need to bring manufacturing back to this country — we live in the Motor City," she said. "I remember back in the day we had hundreds of small companies, small factories. That is gone and we need to bring that back here. And I believe that John James and Mike Rogers will facilitate that." Shortly before 9 a.m. Sahar Haddad, 64, of Dearborn said she’s voted for Democrats previously in her life but now votes Republican. She voted for Rogers at Dearborn’s Lowrey Middle School. "He’s been in politics a long time, so he’s got experience," she said. Hard-fought, ugly and expensive The campaign for Peters' seat was expensive, ugly and hard-fought from the start. At the end, it was rocked by the unprecedented decision of U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens, a centrist Democrat who had lost the nomination to El-Sayed in August but voiced support for him after the primary, to endorse Rogers the Sunday before the election , arguing that El-Sayed hadn't addressed the concerns of Jewish Democrats and had rejected her help. Excoriated for making the switch, Stevens, a four-term congresswoman who had previously criticized Rogers as a "rubber stamp" for President Donald Trump's agenda, was criticized by all corners of her party, her political career likely effectively over. Republicans praised her, and Trump invited her to join the GOP, but it was unclear what effect if any her much-publicized switch made since absentee and early voting had been underway for weeks. But that was merely the last shot fired in a battle unlike any seen for a U.S. Senate seat — and perhaps any statewide seat — in Michigan. According to Open Secrets, which tracks political spending, more than $300 million in spending by groups outside Michigan and independent of the campaigns flooded the airwaves with ads in the state, and the candidates raised more than $100 million combined. Those numbers were preliminary and were expected to grow. While Rogers, who served in Congress from 2001-2015 and is a former House Intelligence Committee chair who had been an occasional critic of Trump's before adopting his agenda and winning his endorsement in 2024 and this year, largely had the Republican nomination to himself, the Democrats had a fractious three-way fight to decide the nomination. Ahead of the August primary, state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, D-Royal Oak, dropped out of the race, confronted by more than $30 million which pro-Israel groups, including organizations linked with the American-Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC , spent on behalf of Stevens, a staunch defender of Israel who after the primary got engaged to a lawyer and prominent Jewish Democrat, Jason Turkish. AIPAC's main target, and Stevens', was El-Sayed, however. El-Sayed, a harsh critic of Israel and its treatment of Palestinians, called for a halt to military aid to that country and was criticized for campaigning with Internet streamer Hasan Piker, who in turn had been chastised for previous anti-Israel comments some Jews called antisemitic (which Piker denied). But he clearly benefited from a growing movement in the Democratic Party that questioned aid to Israel and the Netanyahu government's counteroffensive against Hamas in Gaza. El-Sayed himself was called antisemitic by some, but he routinely and consistently denounced antisemitism and political violence of any kind, while arguing that Israel is engaged in "genocide" and that military spending abroad would be better spent inside the United States on access to health care, education and other priorities. But El-Sayed had more than that going for him. A Michigan native who attended the University of Michigan and trained as a medical doctor but turned to public health rather than practicing medicine, El-Sayed is a progressive firebrand, and a powerful orator, engaging his audiences with infectious rhetoric and an easy-to-remember message that he never wavered from: "Money out of politics, money in your pocket, Medicare for All." With supporters including U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont, U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York and the UAW, he beat Stevens in the Democratic primary by a narrow margin , despite being favored in the polls by a much larger one. But the stage was set and Rogers and his allies set about defining El-Sayed more directly as a "radical" who was out of step with Michigan voters and values, sympathetic to terrorist groups and a socialist. For his part, El-Sayed attempted to remain on message, he and his allies running dozens of ads and the Democratic nominee repeatedly arguing that the election was not about his name or his ethnicity but the cost of fuel pushed to record highs by Trump's war with Iran, a tariff war with Canada that was uniquely hurting Michigan businesses, access to health care and the need to get corporate money out of politics. "I've been consistent," El-Sayed said on Sunday, Nov. 1, as the Stevens endorsement of Rogers broke. "I want to get money out of politics. I want to put money back in pockets. I want Medicare for all. I want to take on the heinous price of gas, the ridiculous price of groceries, the fact that people in the richest, most powerful country in the world cannot see a doctor. The notion that we should continue to breathe, unclean air or unclean water. That has been the focus of this campaign since April of 2025, when we kicked it off." Claims of antisemitism and Islamophobia hung over the race But the concerns of some Jewish voters remained a central theme of the campaign. One group of rabbis and other Jewish leaders called on El-Sayed to not only denounce antisemitism, which he had already done, but also voice support for Israel's self-sovereignty in the Middle East , which he did not given his earlier arguments that Palestinians deserve to be safe and receive humanitarian treatment in their own homes as well, and that the Netanyahu government had denied them that. El-Sayed also declined to denounce Piker, while decrying several of his more incendiary and controversial remarks. He was criticized for not more strongly denouncing ads like one, not put out by his campaign but aired briefly by a supportive group, that linked the price of groceries to U.S. support for Israel in Gaza and elsewhere. El-Sayed noted it was not his ad and he did not agree with its content, however. Significantly, El-Sayed did during one debate with Rogers refuse to say whether he considered Iran or Israel more of a threat to the United States, calling the question "a ridiculous hypothetical." It remained an open question whether Jewish Democrats would vote against him en masse, perhaps defecting to Rogers, as some — including Stevens' fiance — indicated they would. Rogers courted that vote, as well as the vote of Black Detroiters after Stevens won the primary in that city while losing statewide, claiming throughout that he was making inroads. More than that, however, Rogers and his allies ran an aggressive campaign of attempting to denigrate El-Sayed's character, including attempts to link him with the Muslim Brotherhood, though he had never been part of that organization and denounced it on the campaign trail "absolutely." Misleading claims trying to link El-Sayed with groups that some of his and his wife's family members had been involved with that were in turn mentioned as being connected with potential terrorist groups were made by Rogers and his campaign as well, despite the fact that there was no evidence El-Sayed himself was directly associated with those groups or that he or his wife's relatives were in any way connected with wrongdoing or terrorism. In some cases, the campaign became far uglier than that, as Trump himself began calling El-Sayed "Mohammed" as an apparent slur and U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, called him a "jihadist" who would try to institute Islamic religious law, despite a lack of any evidence supporting either claim. Cruz even said that American lives could be at stake if El-Sayed were given a senator's security clearance to sensitive information, in what appeared to be a blatantly prejudiced remark given he has made no similar accusation we're aware of to a non-Muslim candidate. In a state with a large Arab-American and Muslim community such a strategy was risky. Rogers repeatedly said himself that he wasn't questioning El-Sayed's faith or ethnic background but his connections and sympathies. And in some cases, those questions seemed warranted, especially by Jewish Democrats and their allies who were incensed when, in remarks he later retracted, El-Sayed said "hurt people, hurt people" in response to an attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield. (El-Sayed later acknowledged it was the wrong thing to say.) He was repeatedly asked to denounce Piker's remarks, and did so, such as when Piker compared El-Sayed's workers knocking on doors for support in West Bloomfield to a Black civil rights activist looking for support among Ku Klux Klan households, though he never denounced Piker specifically. "His biggest funders are from a group that supports the Muslim Brotherhood. He gets money from people who support openly Hamas, Hezbollah, Al Qaeda," Rogers said at one point in a debate at WOOD-TV in Grand Rapids in early October so fractious that moderator Rick Albin said he had never seen anything like it. Rogers went on to ask for support from anyone willing to "stop a guy who can't condemn terrorism in our own country because he's so close to the people who are supporting the Muslim Brotherhood." But even when El-Sayed did denounce the group, Republicans — as he predicted — would not let it go. Rogers had high obstacles to overcome But Rogers had his own obstacles to contend with, and they weren't minor ones. Despite having lost a narrow election for an open U.S. Senate seat in 2024 to then-U.S. Rep. Elissa Slotkin, Rogers was facing not only the historical fact that the party in power — in this case the Republicans — tends to lose seats in midterm elections like this one, but also high fuel prices caused by the Iran war, a much-maligned tariff war with Canada waged by Trump and the president's poor job approval ratings. Some Republicans, like former FOX News host Tucker Carlson, maligned Rogers as being a product of the "deep state," and spoke in defense of some of El-Sayed's statements. Rogers made a late attempt to break with Trump on the war, saying on Sept. 21 that it needed to "end quickly," because of the effect it was having on increased prices, and, on Trump's tariff war with Canada in early October . Given that he had defended both, and continued to argue justifications for them afterward, his position was criticized by Democrats as equivocal and flipflopping for reasons of political expediency, not an actual breaking with Trump. Meanwhile, establishment Democrats, from Gov. Gretchen Whitmer and others who had endorsed Stevens, coalesced behind El-Sayed. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, who El-Sayed has said he'd like to see replaced, endorsed him. Former President Barack Obama campaigned with him in Detroit on Oct. 24, saying: "Whenever a movement builds to challenge that broken system, the people who benefit from the status quo will say and do anything to stop that train from coming," he said. "They will use lies and they will use fear, and they will use division, and they may even use your name or your faith to somehow suggest that you are dangerous and less than trustworthy, and less patriotic and less American then they are." "We have seen this movie before. I starred in it. I've got a long form birth certificate to prove it. This stuff didn't work on me, not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul," Obama said. The following day, on Oct. 25, Trump campaigned for Rogers and other Republicans in Port Huron, defending the war in Iran and again repeating false claims about El-Sayed. In the last few weeks, polls, which had been within the margin of error, appeared to showed the Democratic nominee expanding his lead, though it still appeared the election could be up for grabs. By Nov. 3, the RealClearPolling.com average of polls showed El-Sayed ahead 5.3-percentage points and, more than that, a series of recent polls had shown him building bigger and bigger leads on Rogers. The Republican, meanwhile, claimed that the early vote model his campaign put together showed him 7 points ahead of El-Sayed, suggesting he could win if the model was correct and his supporters turned out on Election Day. It never materialized. "They turned this race into a simple choice," El-Sayed said. "They want an America that's too small for some us. We know America is big enough for all of us." articles.title: Democrats win Texas governor and Senate races for first time in decades
articles.summary: Talarico defeated the state’s attorney general Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump (Brandon Bell) Democrat James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminarian who campaigned on a "politics of love," on Tuesday won the US Senate race in Texas, dealing a historic blow to Republicans that could reshape American politics. Talarico defeated the state's attorney general Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump who was heavily backed by tech billionaire Elon Musk, US media projected. The result was a major setback for Trump, who threw his weight behind Paxton and made the state a campaign priority. "We defeated Goliath," Talarico told a victory rally in Austin, the state capital. "In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world, and the entire Washington, DC establishment," he said. Talarico took aim at billionaires "who own the social media algorithms, who own the cable news networks, who own the politicians fighting on our screens" and who "want us at each other’s throats." In another political earthquake for the deeply conservative southern border state, Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseated incumbent Texas Governor Greg Abbott. Talarico and Hinojosa are the first Democrats to win statewide office in Texas since 1994. Hinojosa, a 52-year-old attorney and state lawmaker, is part of a new generation of Democrats who are seeking to attract independents and voters disillusioned by Trump’s unpopular war in the Middle East and skyrocketing prices for gas and everyday goods. Thousands of supporters gathered at a watch party in Austin erupted in joy as the results came in, many of them crying and hugging. Some chanted "Si se puede" ("Yes we can" in Spanish), while drivers passing by honked their horns in celebration. "It’s a huge win for Texas, but it’s a giant win for the United States, having James Talarico in the Senate to try to wrest control of this government that's out of control," said Kathy Jackoway, an Austin resident in her 60s. "Everybody is suffering. Everybody is hurting, and Trump is busy building monuments to himself." Anisha, 29, said she hoped the two Democrats would govern "for everyone, not just the billionaires, not just the elite." - 'Mandate the size of Texas' - The landmark victories for Democrats could signal that Texas, the country’s second most populous state with 40 electoral votes, is becoming competitive in national elections, a shift that could reshape the electoral map for future races. "This is a win the size of Texas and now we have a mandate the size of Texas," Talarico said. The results mark a bruising defeat for Musk, who spent more than $200 million to support Talarico’s rival, according to federal filings. The world's richest man, Musk has moved the headquarters of Tesla, SpaceX and X to Texas. The spread of AI data centers across Texas became a central issue in both races, as residents worried about rising electricity bills, water use and strain on the power grid. Talarico and Hinojosa both called for tighter regulation, prompting Abbott, a longtime champion of the industry, to propose new rules of his own. Talarico ran on a blend of Christian faith and economic populism, describing the contest as a David versus Goliath fight and inviting Republicans dissatisfied with the party to join him. Trump traveled to Texas four times in the month before the election to rally for Paxton, whom he endorsed over four-term incumbent senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary. Talarico, 37, was elected to the Texas House of Representatives in 2018 and built a national following with speeches combining progressive politics, biblical teaching and criticism of wealthy elites. He defeated congresswoman Jasmine Crockett in the Democratic primary and sought to broaden his appeal by criticizing aspects of former president Joe Biden’s immigration policies. Paxton, 63, survived impeachment by the Republican-controlled Texas House in 2023 on allegations of corruption and abuse of power before being acquitted by the state Senate. He has denied wrongdoing. articles.title: 'I wasn't on the ballot': Trump distances himself from GOP midterm losses
articles.summary: President Donald Trump sought to distance himself from Republicans' mounting midterm losses Tuesday, declaring in his first remarks on the election results that his party would have been victorious had he been on the ballot. "I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" Trump wrote on social media. Trump's efforts to sidestep blame for the growing blue wave came as Republicans were dealt stunning losses in deep red states and districts, with Democrats flipping Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Ohio. Republicans also lost Senate races in North Carolina and Georgia, and are trailing in other key contests. Trump told the New York Times that he is "absolutely willing to accept" the election results. “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out," Trump said. Democrats are poised to flip both chambers of Congress by wide margins, with the party seizing on backlash to Trump's second-term agenda, including concerns about his handling of the economy and the Iran war. Despite his record-low approval rating, Trump thrust himself into the center of the midterm election with a series of rallies across 20 states in the closing weeks. The midterm contests are shaping up to be an emphatic repudiation of a president who implored voters to "pretend" he was on the ballot. articles.title: Democrat Amy Acton wins Ohio governor's race, ending 20-year GOP streak
articles.summary: Dr. Amy Acton speaks at a campaign rally in Toledo, Ohio, on Oct. 29, 2026. —Michael M. Santiago—Getty Images Dr. Amy Acton will be Ohio’s next governor, defeating her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy in a heated race that has gained national attention in recent weeks over a controversial attack-ad against the Democrat. On Tuesday evening, AP called the race for Acton, who previously served as the director of the state’s health department during the COVID-19 pandemic, reporting that she won 50.8% of the vote with 86% of votes counted. Ramaswamy, who was backed by President Donald Trump, earned 45.9% of the vote, according to AP. Acton’s victory marks the first time in two decades that Ohioans have elected a Democrat to the governorship. It represents a significant blow to Republicans, who initially liked their chances in a state that the President won by double digits in the 2024 election. Ramaswamy attack ad sparks widespread controversy The race, which was an open battle since current Republican Gov. Mike DeWine was restricted from running again because of term limits, took a striking turn in the lead-up to Election Day. The Cook Political Report had previously rated the race as “Lean Republican,” but later adjusted its analysis and marked it a “Toss Up.” On Oct. 23, though, the Cook Political Report shifted the race slightly in Democrats’ favor to “Lean Democrat.” The election forecaster attributed its latest assessment in part to an attack ad released by  Ramaswamy’s campaign in October. The ad featured Acton’s estranged mother, who lost custody of Acton and her brother in 1978, the same year that their stepfather was indicted on charges of raping Acton when she was a child. It sparked backlash across the political aisle. Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, described the ad as “a despicable low.” “It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Stearns said in a statement . “This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core—a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants.” The state’s current Republican governor said that the ad was “deeply, deeply troubling” and “just plain wrong,” calling for Ramaswamy’s campaign to rescind it. DeWine maintained, nonetheless, that he still endorsed Ramaswamy and “the whole [Republican] ticket.” But Ramaswamy, who launched an unsuccessful bid for the Republican nomination in the 2024 election, doubled down on the ad. Both Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance defended him in the wake of the outrage. articles.title: Trump says U.S. is ready to strike Iran as negotiators struggle to reach deal
articles.summary: By Parisa Hafezi and Jana Choukeir DUBAI, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Iran and the United States are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, as US President Donald Trump declined to rule out a resumption of US combat operations after the elections in the United States. Trump made his comments in separate interviews as Americans voted in ‌pivotal midterm elections in which the unpopular Iran war has been a key factor and as mediator Qatar stepped up efforts to avert a renewed escalation. Overnight, the United States carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's ‌Qeshm island, targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations. Trump on Tuesday renewed warnings of military action in an interview with the Fox News Channel. "I'm not looking ​to ... kill lots of people," he said. "If we have to, we'll have to." In an interview with the Financial Times, Trump suggested he was content with the state of the stand-off with Iran. "We seem to be getting everything we want," the paper quoted him as saying in a six-minute telephone interview. The FT said it asked Trump about what it called "strong hints" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be an attack later this week. "I’m ready, we’re ready. We’re locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," he replied. Trump told the FT indirect negotiations with Iran about its stockpile of enriched uranium were ongoing. "We’re having discussions, and we’ll see how that all works out," ‌he said. Also on Tuesday, Trump made a surprise announcement of a deal with ⁠Netanyahu under which Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after this year, but would sell weapons to its close Middle East ally. The remarks appeared aimed at swaying voters unhappy with US support for Israel. Fears have grown that the conflict launched by the United States and Israel in February could flare up again after Tuesday's midterms. "Mediators are ⁠working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington," the senior Iranian official said, speaking on condition of anonymity. Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of a draft US-Iran deal discussed over the past eight days. "Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened," the Iranian official cautioned, referring to Iranian demands including waiving oil sanctions, ending the US naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian funds. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, later said ​the ​US response to Iranian demands "was not convincing", adding that Washington "must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them". "Only ​in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened," he wrote on X. 'WE CANNOT ‌LOSE HOPE' Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said both the United States and Iran were reviewing proposals put forward by mediators. While the Qatari team that travelled to Tehran had returned to Doha, talks were continuing. "There are intensive joint regional efforts underway to avoid escalation," he told a news briefing, adding that Qatar remained hopeful a deal could still be reached to pave the way for future negotiations. "If there were no glimmer of hope, there would be no negotiations... and as a mediator, we cannot lose hope," he said. An official briefed on the talks said feedback from Washington and Tehran was expected within the next 36 hours. A senior Iranian official told Reuters later on Tuesday that there is no deadline for exchanging messages with Washington through mediators or reviewing responses. 'FORCEFUL RESPONSE' The senior Iranian official said Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands" and that nuclear talks could begin only after Iran's conditions were met. Tehran would respond ‌forcefully, in the region and beyond, to US strikes, the official added. Oil prices slipped in early trade on Wednesday as investors ​awaited the results of the midterm elections and their potential impact on peace talks, even after industry data showed US crude stocks unexpectedly ​fell last week. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said the ball was in Washington's court after a "strong ​and rational response" from Tehran. "The enemy seeks to force the Iranian nation into submission through threats and military action, but they are sorely mistaken; Iran will not submit," Qalibaf said. ‌He said Tehran's response to any US miscalculation would be unpredictable and unconstrained by ​geography. The head of Iran's armed forces general staff, Ali Abdollahi, ​said Iran's military was updating target lists that included US and Israeli assets and would respond immediately to any threat. Hardline newspaper Kayhan said on Tuesday that US facilities in Britain, Italy, Greece, Romania, Albania and Cyprus could be targeted in the event of renewed war. IRANIAN-SAUDI TALKS Alongside indirect exchanges between Tehran and Washington, regional powers are pursuing diplomatic efforts to prevent further escalation. The conflict has also widened, with Yemen's Iran-aligned ​Houthis stepping up attacks on Saudi Arabia. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Tuesday ‌talks with Saudi Arabia were continuing to seek new regional security arrangements that would exclude foreign military involvement. Last week, senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian counterparts in Tehran, ​the first such high-level contacts since August. (Additional reporting by Nayera Abdallah, Tala Ramadan and Elwely Elwelly in Dubai, Andrew Mills in Doha, Doina Chiacu and David Brunnstrom in Washington, Yasmine Ghania in ​Cairo; Writing by Dubai Newsroom and Tom Perry, Editing by Raju Gopalakrishnan, Ros Russell, Don Durfee and Kate Mayberry) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://uk.news.yahoo.com/irans-foreign-minister-says-talks-071254829.html

articles.title: A rare condition killed a 24-year-old first-time NYC Marathon runner. Its warning signs can be easy to miss.
articles.summary: Just two miles short of the finish line of the 2026 New York City Marathon on Nov. 1, 24-year-old runner Rachel Apa collapsed. She died of a rare and potentially life-threatening illness that can be brought on by excessive exertion, the New York Times reported. It's called rhabdomyolysis , and while there are relatively few cases nationwide each year, it can strike during endurance or intensive exercise, including marathons. What happened to Rachel Apa? Apa was running her first marathon to raise money for Parkinson's disease in honor of her late grandfather, according to the New York Times. But Apa was no stranger to athletics, having played Division I field hockey in college. Her family said Apa had been in "perfect health." Plus, she'd been training for the race for months. But at mile 18, Apa texted her father, Steve, who'd been checking in at each mile: "Ow." At the end of the next mile, she wrote, "Ow ow." She stopped responding after that. Apa's mother, Michelle, was at the race and had watched her daughter run by earlier on. Her parents noticed on the marathon tracking app that Apa stopped moving after mile 24. Apa collapsed just after running past hospital social worker Michaela Nichols, who was cheering on participants. Nichols ran over and checked Apa's pulse, but couldn't find one. Three other people — two of whom said they were physicians — ran over to give Apa CPR. Marathon medical staff tried to revive her with a defibrillator before an ambulance arrived. She was taken to Mount Sinai Medical Center and treated for six hours, but could not be saved. Her father told the New York Times that Apa's cause of death was rhabdomyolysis. What is rhabdomyolysis? It's a dangerous medical condition that occurs when skeletal muscle (the kind that connects to bones and allows you to move) gets damaged and rapidly breaks down. "The internal components of muscle cells, which include various electrolytes, proteins and enzymes, spill out, and those in turn can be toxic to the kidneys and dangerous to the heart," Dr. David Mariuma , a nephrologist at Stony Brook Medicine who was not involved in Apa's treatment, tells Yahoo. Specifically, the released molecules can lead to kidney failure and life-threatening heart arrhythmias if not treated quickly and properly. This destructive process can be triggered in several different ways. The most common cause is not exercise, but injury, according to the Cleveland Clinic. Traumatic crushing injuries are the most likely to induce rhabdomyolysis (often referred to as simply "rhabdo"), but severe burns or electrocution can also lead to muscle breakdown. Cleveland Clinic reports that there are about 26,000 total cases of rhabdomyolysis in the U.S. each year. It's harder to say exactly how many are due to exercise, but one study estimates that physical exertion — including endurance athletic activities, manual labor and intense exercise — may account for up to 47% of cases. The true number is likely higher, Mariuma says. Who is at risk? Although it's uncommon, anyone can develop rhabdomyolysis, regardless of age and athletic experience. Dr. Jessica Tomazic , a sports and exercise medicine staff physician with the Cleveland Clinic who was not involved in Apa's care nor familiar with her case, tells Yahoo that a combination of risk factors can increase the likelihood. They include: Dehydration Heat, or temperatures one is not accustomed to exercising in Being sick Certain genetic conditions, including sickle cell disease Recent consumption of alcohol Drug use (particularly cocaine, according to Mariuma) Prior heat illness, rhabdomyolysis or a family history of rhabdo Rhabdomyolysis is also more common among men, people who smoke and those with obesity. In rare cases, certain medications, including statins, can lead to the condition when the dose is too high for an individual patient, says Mariuma. Higher rates of rhabdomyolysis have also been linked to endurance athletes, spin classes and high-intensity interval training, including the P90X workout program. And researchers have looked specifically at cases of rhabdo among New York City marathon runners. An Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai study identified at least one rhabdo incident each year between 2017 and 2024 (excluding 2020, when the marathon was canceled due to COVID). Twenty-one-year-old Austin Stallman died of rhabdomyolysis after collapsing during a 9-mile Navy SEAL training run in Texas earlier in 2026. "This is the kind of thing where sometimes everything could go right, you could do everything you're supposed to do and it still happens," says Mariuma. What are the symptoms? The condition can be hard to spot because many of its symptoms are similar to what some people experience during intense physical challenges. It typically begins with soreness or pain that feels more extreme than usual for the activity, according to Mariuma and Tomiazic. Pain is especially concerning if it's accompanied by more weakness than normal or "any sense of confusion, nausea, or what we call constitutional symptoms that are not specific to the muscle — a general sense that something is off, or malaise," says Mariuma. Another telltale sign is dark urine, the color of tea or soda, he adds. But a marathon runner is unlikely to detect this signal mid-race. How to prevent rhabdomyolysis — and what to do if it happens Gradually training for a new activity, rather than jumping in at full tilt, can help reduce the risk. It's also important to stay hydrated not only during but also leading up to and after an activity that requires a lot of exertion, both experts advise. And if you're feeling at all unwell, stay home or at least keep your physical activity light, as intense activity while sick is a risk factor for the condition. Tomazic, who is also a trail runner and ski patroller, acknowledges that the symptoms and risk factors — such as not properly fueling with water and food — can be easy to lose track of, especially mid-competition. "We — I say we because I do these things — we tend to push through pain; that's the mindset that we're encouraged to take," Tomazic says. "So sometimes it can be difficult to determine, 'Is this a pain that I should really listen to, or is it a pain that I can monitor, for now?'" If you notice any symptoms of rhabdomyolysis, acting quickly is important, especially if you have risk factors for the condition, because "when it happens, it tends to happen over minutes to hours," says Mariuma. You should stop what you're doing, call for help and try to find some shade if you're outside on a hot day, Tomazic says. Staying well hydrated helps dilute and flush out myoglobin, the muscle protein that can build up during rhabdomyolysis, and other molecules. But he adds, don't overdo it on plain water. Make sure you're getting electrolytes from your diet or sports drinks during intense athletic activities, since too much water without them can cause a dangerous condition called hyponatremia . Rhabdomyolysis is primarily treated with IV fluids, which help the kidneys clear myoglobin and other substances released from damaged muscles. In cases where the kidneys have already suffered damage, some patients may receive dialysis, according to the Cleveland Clinic. More than 90% of patients who don't develop kidney damage from rhabdo survive, but the fatality rate rises to more than 20% with kidney injury, according to one study. But overall, both Tomazic and Mariuma say that rhabdo shouldn't discourage you from running or participating in the physical activities you want to do. "Exercise-related rhabdo is rare … so I wouldn't use a tragedy like this as a reason to not do a marathon," says Mariuma. "Any activity out there, there are risks, and the only thing we can really do is learn the best ways to prevent them." articles.title: Tennessee murderer captured in Missouri after prison escape and truck theft
articles.summary: Authorities have captured a convicted murderer who evaded law enforcement for more than a week after escaping from a Tennessee prison. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation announced Tuesday that Jacob Morley was back in custody. He was arrested near Kansas City, Missouri, investigators said. "Thank you to the public for your assistance, vigilance, and the tips provided during this investigation," the bureau said in a statement. "We also thank all of our law enforcement partners for their continued efforts to safely bring this search to a successful conclusion." Investigators got a tip Tuesday morning that Morley had been hiding in a shed at a hunting camp around Marion, Illinois, some 320 miles south of Chicago, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said in a statement. Authorities also learned a truck had been stolen from the property. Missouri State Highway Patrol said it handled Morley's arrest alongside multiple partner agencies, after Tennessee authorities reported that Morley may be traveling through Missouri, based on footage obtained through Flock cameras. The arrest happened around 11:30 a.m. local time near Norborne, a small city about an hour's drive from Kansas City, the state agency said. Authorities said they also recovered three firearms that had previously been reported stolen inside the truck. Little information about the inmate's escape and the multi-state search for him has been made available since Morley broke out of prison. But investigators said more will be released as it becomes available. Morley, 28, was serving a life sentence at the Northwest Correctional Complex in an isolated part of Tiptonville, a town roughly 90 miles from Memphis in northwestern Tennessee. He had been convicted of killing a coworker four years ago, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. Correctional officers discovered Morley was missing from the prison at around 11:30 p.m. local time on Oct. 25, the department said. While parsing security cameras later on, investigators said they saw footage of Morley escaping the complex while wearing his prison uniform by slipping through a fence on the property. Authorities released additional security footage two days later that showed the inmate stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350, with Tennessee plates and a logo for Lindamood Planting Company on the side door, in the early hours of Oct. 27. It was stolen from Lake County, which includes Tiptonville, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said. The truck was located later the same day in Marion, Illinois, which is about 150 miles north of Tiptonville, the investigative bureau said . Morley's whereabouts were unknown at the time. The bureau had said earlier in the week that Morley was on its "most wanted" list, as various agencies, including the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, the governor's office and U.S. Marshals, offered combined rewards of up to $17,500 for information leading to his arrest. Investigators haven't shared details about how exactly the inmate escaped, beyond the fact that he breached a fence at the prison. Morley received a lifetime prison sentence for murdering Cody Birchfield, his former coworker, in 2022. Authorities said Birchfield's body was found in a box under Morley's home in Tennessee's Carter County after he had been missing for several weeks. In addition to first-degree murder, Morley was convicted of aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, vandalism and evading arrest, as he fled when deputies arrived at his home in 2022. Authorities said the manhunt for him at the time ended in North Carolina. Northwest Correctional Complex is a men's prison with the capacity to hold 1,776 inmates under varying degrees of security, from the lowest level up to maximum, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. It also houses minors who have been convicted of crimes as adults. Multiple violent incidents have taken place inside the prison in recent years, some of which involved attacks between inmates and prison staff. In July, a grand jury returned dozens of indictments over the murders of five inmates, assaults against staff and other acts of violence. At a recent meeting of the Tennessee Inmate Disciplinary Oversight Board, members discussed ongoing problems in the prison and suggested issues with leadership played a role. articles.title: Tail component broke off before deadly Florida jet crash, investigators say
articles.summary: Investigators continue to work to “gather critical evidence” of what caused a Bahamas-bound Learjet to crash in Palm Beach County, Fla., on Nov. 1. At a Nov. 3 National Transportation Safety Board press conference, spokesperson Tom Chapman called the investigation a "big puzzle to try to put together,” with work at the impact site hampered by severe storms. The NTSB will be working with local public works teams this week to remove water from the crater caused by the plane’s impact, where investigators expect to find airplane components that will help determine what went wrong. Chapman had one notable development to share: The aircraft's left elevator — a control surface on the tail that controls the up-and-down pitch of the plane — was found in three pieces between about 1.3 and 3.8 miles from the crash site. Investigators believe it separated from the plane before impact. Chapman urged members of the public who find wreckage not to touch it and to call authorities. Weather remains a key focus of the investigation, Chapman said. He also appeared to rule out a connection between the crash and the plane's proximity to President Trump's Mar-a-Lago Club. Earlier in the day, Jeff Gregory, 55, of Gilbertsville, Penn., was identified as the plane's pilot. The crash killed all nine people aboard,  including his copilot, Nathalia Filgueiras , and seven passengers, Fox 29 reports . The families of Filgueiras and the passengers had previously confirmed their deaths. Camila Corteleti identified her 20-year-old daughter as one of the pilots of the private jet, the New York Times reported. A joint statement from the families was released on social media. "With broken hearts, our families share that Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp, their children Emma and Charlie, Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr and Anita Maria Cetina were among those lost aboard the flight that went down near Greenacres, Florida, on November 1," the statement said. A tribute to Sharp and her family was posted on her Instagram page , saying, "On behalf of friends and family, it is with a heavy heart that we share that our dearest Helen was taken from us too soon. If you knew Helen, you knew how full of life she was. She simply radiated." In a news conference on Nov. 2, investigators said weather conditions were a major factor in the federal investigation into the fatal crash. The NTSB told reporters on Nov. 2 that ice was forming on the jet as it experienced moderate turbulence. Miami air traffic control granted the pilot permission to climb from 35,000 feet to 37,000 feet to avoid precipitation, but shortly afterward, an emergency was declared with a mayday call. Air traffic control audio posted on LiveATC captured the crew's comments leading up to the crash. Someone in the cockpit can be heard saying "Mayday, mayday," reporting the plane was descending at 10,000 feet per minute, Reuters reported. "We're going to crash into the ground," the person, since identified as Filgueiras, said. The Learjet 60, which had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas, went down at about 12:50 p.m. ET near Cresthaven, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. A man who was leaving the area of the crash sustained a leg injury, officials said. Dashcam footage posted to social media by an eyewitness showed the aircraft falling toward the ground beside a road and exploding into a fireball, narrowly missing cars and homes. The impact left a "massive crater" near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at a news conference. About 600 residents were evacuated to two shelters, he said. People stand near a crater formed after the Learjet 60 crashed. Vanessa Lara/via REUTERS "We have a lot of work to do on scene — this will be a several-day process," NTSB senior investigator Timothy Monville said during Nov. 2's news conference. "The biggest obstacle we're going to have is recovering the major wreckage from the impacted crater on the roadway." The NTSB said it will interview witnesses to the accident as part of its investigation and encouraged anyone with relevant information, videos or audio to contact the NTSB by email at witness@ntsb.gov. Chapman also told reporters that, according to records, a cockpit voice recorder was installed, but the NTSB doesn't know whether it was still on board. "Sometimes these things change over time," Chapman said. "Of course we're very hopeful that we can recover it. Too early to know, but that will be very important data." What we know about the victims Among the victims was the private jet's pilot, Gregory, a husband and father from Gilbertsville, Pa., outside Philadelphia. Federal Aviation Administration records obtained by the Associated Press say he held airline transport pilot and flight instructor certificates. Friends described Gregory as a devout Christian. They believe his was the voice heard reciting a prayer in the background of Filgueiras's final radio transmissions to air traffic control as the plane descended, the AP reports. Thomas Noetzel, director of operations at Upper Jets, the company that operated the flight, organized an online fundraiser to support Gregory's wife and children. "Jeff was also a personal friend, and knowing him has made me a better person," Noetzel wrote. Gregory's former employer, East Coast Jets, a private jet company in Allentown, said he was an aviator with years of experience , according to the New York Times. He worked there in 2016 and 2017. "We are deeply saddened to learn that Captain Jeff Gregory was among those who lost their lives in yesterday's tragic aviation accident in Palm Beach," a spokesperson for East Coast Jets said in a statement on Nov. 2. His copilot Filgueiras's mother said she earned her pilot's license at age 17. The 20-year-old had logged more than 1,300 hours of flight time and was working for a private charter firm based in Fort Lauderdale, according to her mother. Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras itsnatfilg/Threads NFL running back Joe Mixon was among those paying tribute to Gregory and Filgueiras . In an X post on Nov. 3, the former Pro Bowler said he had recently flown with the pilots on the very same aircraft. "They were incredible professionals and genuinely wonderful people," Mixon, who most recently played for the Houston Texans, wrote. He added, "My heart, thoughts, and prayers go out to the grieving families and loved ones of everyone on board. A tragic reminder of how fragile life is. Love on your loved ones while you can, because you never know what tomorrow may bring." Absolutely devastated by yesterday’s tragic plane crash in Florida and the loss of all nine lives. I flew on that exact aircraft last month with those same two pilots. They were incredible professionals and genuinely wonderful people. Hearing the young woman’s story and learning… — ⚡️Primetime!!!⚡️ (@Joe_MainMixon) November 2, 2026 According to the Palm Beach Post , the crash also killed Helen Sharp, 40, her husband, Adam Robinson, 45, and their two young children. Sharp's father, 70-year-old Dudley Sharp, confirmed the deaths to the outlet. "It's quite a blow," he told the Palm Beach Post. "We had a daughter, her husband and two grandchildren on the plane." Family members of the seven passengers killed in the Nov. 1 crash released a joint statement on Facebook that also identifies the other three passengers: Anita Maria Cetina, Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr. "With broken hearts, our families share that Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp, their children Emma and Charlie, Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, and Anita Maria Cetina were among those lost aboard the flight that went down near Greenacres, Florida, on November 1," the statement said. "Adam and Helen were devoted parents, and Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were the light of their lives.  Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last forever.  Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives.  Their loss will be felt deeply by all those who loved them and who they loved in return." "Charmi and Rachel were full of joy and adventure," the statement continued. "They loved their people fiercely, fully and without hesitation. From the moment they met, they were all in on each other and the life they were building. They are deeply loved, and we will miss them endlessly. Anita Maria cared for Emma and Charlie with tenderness and devotion, and she was truly part of the family.  She showed us a legacy of unconditional love and devotion." Reed and Fehr were hailed as “two extraordinary individuals” in a post from the Arca Boutique Hotel in Honduras, which they co-owned. View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram The families also thanked first responders, investigators and the Palm Beach community for "their care," as well as "everyone who reached out with love." They added: "Our hearts are also with the families of the pilots, who are grieving alongside us." Robinson was a tech entrepreneur from Austin, according to his LinkedIn page. He described himself as the founder and CEO for RB2B and Retention.com. He also once hosted the podcast Ten Years in the Making , in which he shared conversations with e-commerce founders. In one 2023 episode with former aviation entrepreneur Lolita Petrossov, Robinson spoke about how flying private "became part of my identity." A fellow tech entrepreneur, Jesse Ouellette, shared a tribute on LinkedIn, saying Robinson had helped him when he was building his company. "He became a friend and someone I saw eye to eye with on how to build software companies," said Ouellette. "He could disagree with you about almost anything, and somehow you'd walk away liking him even more." Robinson last posted on LinkedIn on the day of his death, promoting a debate he and Ouellette had scheduled for Nov. 3. Sharp was a sculptural ceramic artist, according to her Instagram account . A tribute posted on her page said she founded a PR company, Influential PR. The pair, according to the same post, met while Sharp was living abroad in Buenos Aires, Argentina. What we know The aircraft crashed in a residential area in Greenacres. Anadolu via Getty Images The Learjet 60 took off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. FAA records list the owner as a Delaware corporation. The National Weather Service had a flood watch in effect for the crash area, Palm Beach County, through Nov. 2, with rain expected on and off across South Florida. In air traffic control audio posted on LiveATC, someone in the cockpit said they were "managing the ice" but faced "moderate" turbulence and were seeking "better rides." The Associated Press reported the crew also asked to climb. Less than a minute later, the person said "Mayday, mayday," reporting the plane was suddenly descending at 10,000 feet per minute. Seconds later, the person declared an emergency, with the descent rate reaching 20,000 feet per minute. Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: "We're going to crash into the ground," before reporting the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane began to bank. Flightradar24 data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute. The last words heard from the cockpit were "we're out of time." Driver Aki Kuusisto's dashcam footage captured the moment the jet hit the ground. "I heard a whistling noise, a big bang, and I saw a fireball," he told CBS News . "It felt like it was right next to us... you could feel it in the car." The jet is reported to have descended at a peak of 32,000 feet per minute. Anadolu via Getty Images Accuweather reported that thunderstorms in the area produced heavy rainfall and lightning.  AP reports that the pilots were warned by controllers about the looming storms as they crossed into Florida and the FAA published an official warning about the weather prior to the plane's departure on Nov. 1. According to AccuWeather, the tops of some of the storm clouds reached up to 45,000 feet, making it difficult for planes to fly over. The plane may not have been able to detect the updrafts that can intensify precipitation, as AccuWeather's Dan DePodwin said that the weather radars on planes have limitations. Chapman said that the investigators are yet to determine what the weather conditions were at 35,000 feet, the altitude the plane was flying at when problems were first reported by the copilot.  He added that the investigators hope to recover the cockpit voice recorder. 'A cataclysmic plane crash' Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis told reporters during a Nov. 1 briefing that there was "a lot of debris" that was strewn over a "pretty significant distance." "It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis said. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road." Transportation Secretary Duffy called the crash a "horrific tragedy" and said the FAA and Department of Transportation would be investigating the incident. Anthony Blackmon, who lives around 500 feet from the site of the crash, told NBC Miami that debris from the crash struck his home. "Debris was everywhere," he said. "Debris hit my house. Everything was on fire. The road was on fire. I've always seen it on the news, never thought it would happen so close to somebody like how it happened today." Adam Itayem told WPTV , "It sounded like a loud boom. I thought it was thunder," adding, "I saw a big crater in the ground and water coming out of the crater and a big fire too." "I heard and felt the boom," Andrew Mannino told CNN , saying he saw a "large black cloud immerse in the air," adding, "The power immediately went out and is still out." Around 600 people were evacuated by Palm Beach County authorities while federal officials investigate the crash. "We're waiting for someone to give us answers about what we're going to do, because they're not even letting us into the community to get our clothes," local resident Jesus Solorzano told WPTV. articles.title: 2 people dead, hundreds rescued amid severe flooding in Florida
articles.summary: Two people were killed -- one of whom died in a vehicle -- and hundreds of others were rescued since Sunday as a storm brought severe flooding in Palm Bay, Florida, according to Palm Bay Mayor Rob Medina. The deceased victims have been identified by Florida officials as Joshua Bennett, 34, and Archie Richards, 78 Emergency crews rescued hundreds of people from flooded areas using boats and special high-water vehicles, Medina said in a press conference Tuesday. Port St. Lucie Police Department - PHOTO: In this screen grab from a video posted to social media, a truck travels through flood waters in Port St. Lucie, Fla., on Nov. 3, 2026. Greg Lovett/USA Today Network via Reuters - PHOTO: Workers from A1 Moving move a voting machine out of Magnolia Park Town Hall polling precinct after flooding in the parking lot forced them to move to another location during the US midterm election in Magnolia Park, Fla., on Nov. 3, 2026. Some homes suffered major damage. One family reported that 38 inches of water had filled their living room, Medina told reporters. "That is devastation within our city," Medina said. Officials warned that flooding could continue even after the rain stops because water may take several days to drain. They urged residents to stay away from flooded roads, fast-moving water and downed power lines. Election 2026 live updates: Americans cast their votes Florida Fish & Wildlife - PHOTO: FWC officers have deployed to St. Lucie County to conduct rescue operations and assist residents affected by this week’s historic rainfall and flooding. Flooding has also affected other parts of Florida, including St. Lucie, Martin and Palm Beach counties. State officials said they are working with local leaders to determine how much damage the storm caused. A low-pressure system over the Gulf led to continuous onshore flow over the Florida peninsula on Sunday and Monday. articles.title: 宋雪涛：共和党中选大败有何影响？
articles.summary: 截至北京时间11月4日下午，根据Polymarket数据：众议院435席，民主党:共和党约为260:175；参议院100席，民主党:共和党为56:44；州长50个，民主党:共和党为30:20。 由此，民主党大约获得了60%的众议院席位、55%的参议院席位、60%的州长。 1、中选变得重要起来： 之前普遍认为中选的重要性不够高，主要是因为总统拥有否决权，而民主党不能赢下2/3的席位，所以很难直接推翻过往已经存在的事项。 但现在局势不同，民主党距离2/3并不遥远，这就必须考虑共和党议员反水的情况，特别是对一些明显错误、可能进一步导致28年大选失败的事项。 从现在到1月3日，有两个月的过渡期，用于确认投票结果、党内选举新一届国会领袖等，在此之前，本届国会继续履职。 很多变化可能在过渡期内就会发生。 2、美伊战争可能更快结束： 观察美国舆论，对伊战争并没有得到共和党内的广泛支持，很大程度上是特朗普本人和身边少数亲以色列群体推动的。 之所以此前党内反对声音少，是因为共和党候选人尽力避免在中选前与特朗普唱反调，输掉党内初选。 现在中选即将结束，特朗普也不会有第三任期，如果他一意孤行，推动大规模重启伊朗战争，可能会面临党内，例如建制派议员反水的风险。 根据法律，只要众议院超过半数通过，就可以对总统发起弹劾；如果参议院超过2/3多数，一般是67票通过，就可以成功弹劾总统。 2019年和2021年，特朗普曾两次被众议院发起弹劾，都在参议院被否决。 这一次，如果有11名共和党参议员反水，民主党就可能弹劾成功。 因此，后续两党很可能同步施压要求结束战争，迫使特朗普想办法尽快在过渡期内退出。 3、财政赤字可能不降反升： 早些年前，在野党赢得国会控制权，往往会令执政党达成妥协，约束财政纪律，例如1994年之后的克林顿和2010年之后的奥巴马。 然而如今民粹盛行，两党谁也不敢轻言削减福利，否则很快就被民众反噬。 因此，近十年更常见的情况，是执政党通过允许在野党增加有利赤字，换取不削减执政党赤字，结果就是赤字越来越高。 例如2018年和2022年的中选均导致国会分裂，但次年赤字率都变得更高 美国政府2027财年的预算还没通过，两党将在过渡期内就此展开博弈，如果共和党不让步，政府可能会在年底陷入停摆。 近期民主党众议院领袖已经表态，民主党控制众议院后，前100天优先解决的事项，前两项就是恢复《平价医疗法案》医保保费税收抵免、撤销共和党在2025年法案中削减的Medicaid支出。 4、关注AIDC的地方监管： 由于没有2/3席位，民主党仍然难以在国会层面，即全国层面通过限制AI的法案。 然而在地方层面，共和党州长输掉太多，包括很多AIDC规划建设规模较大的州：德州、俄亥俄、乔治亚、宾州、亚利桑那等。 从选前主张来看，并非所有民主党州长对AIDC的立场都比共和党州长更强硬。 因此，后续是以检验实际政策为主。 本文来源： 雪涛宏观笔记 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 华为、阿里、腾讯、小米、百度、火山引擎等：共同抵制利用智能体实施算法压榨、黑灰产等行为
articles.summary: 11月4日，2026年世界互联网大会乌镇峰会“智能体互信互联互操作全球合作创新——携手构建智能互联网论坛”正式发布了《智能体发展自律公约》（以下简称《自律公约》）。《自律公约》是落实《智能体规范应用与创新发展实施意见》“强化行业自律”任务部署的具体举措，由中国信息通信研究院（简称“中国信通院”）、腾讯、蚂蚁、阿里、抖音等智能体生态主体，在中国网络社会组织联合会等组织下共同起草并发布。 《自律公约》共提出八条自律措施，一是健全智能体信任体系，二是建设智能体互联基础设施，三是提升智能体互操作水平，四是提升智能体安全防护能力，五是健全智能体治理机制，六是保护智能体用户权益，七是加速智能体赋能千行百业，八是推动智能体技术普惠共享。 《自律公约》的制定发布，是智能体行业迈向规范化发展的重要一步，将有利于凝聚各方共识，推动行业加强自律，推动提升智能体互信、互联、互操作水平，引导智能体规范应用、创新发展。 下一步，各发起单位将带头落实《自律公约》约定，主动接受行业组织和社会公众监督。同时，欢迎智能体生态中各类主体积极参与公约建设，共同营造开放、可信、安全、普惠的智能体生态。 附：公约全文及发起单位名单 智能体发展自律公约 智能体是人类智慧的延伸，是增进人类福祉、促进社会进步和可持续发展的工具。为促进智能体互信、互联、互操作，推动规范应用与创新发展，构建开放、可信、安全、普惠的智能体生态，我们共同制定并积极践行本公约，自觉接受行业组织和社会监督。本公约将根据行业发展和政策法规变化定期评估、适时修订，以确保公约的时效性与适用性。 第一条 健全智能体信任体系。建立分层次、可验证的智能体身份标识，完善智能体身份验证与管理、权限授予与控制、规则表达与内嵌等机制。降低智能体互信的技术门槛，为构建智能体生态建立信任锚点。 第二条 建设智能体互联基础设施。共建可互联的基础设施，发展智能体注册与解析、能力描述与发现、意图理解与转换、网络路由与连接、资源调度与计量、协议兼容与互认等技术与标准。不断降低智能体跨域发现连接成本，支撑智能体互联协同。 第三条 提升智能体互操作水平。在合法合规、守牢安全底线前提下，尊重各方知识产权与正当权益，坚持开放协作、平等协商，深化能力开放与接口适配、任务委托与协同执行、分类分级授权与行为边界、权利义务与责任划分等机制。有序降低智能体互操作壁垒，通过多智能体能力整合提升复杂任务交付水平。 第四条 提升智能体安全防护能力。健全前瞻性风险评估、运行监测、行为管控、异常熔断等技术体系，努力保障模型、插件、技能来源可靠，共建风险信息共享与联合处置机制。持续防范人工智能内生缺陷与外部攻击引发智能体越权操作、隐私泄露乃至行为失控等安全风险，打造安全可控的产品服务。 第五条 健全智能体治理机制。积极发展规则表达与内嵌、合规性测试等技术，确保智能体行为遵守法律法规、公序良俗，共同抵制利用智能体实施算法压榨、黑灰产等行为。持续构建健康向善的发展秩序，提升智能体融入经济社会体系的能力。 第六条 保护智能体用户权益。保障用户知情权、选择权和对重要事项的最终控制权，防范个人信息滥用、过度迎合、认知操纵，加强未成年人、老年人等特殊群体保护，培育用户健康使用素养。不断提升智能体公平性与可及性，保障用户在智能体时代平等享有发展权。 第七条 加速智能体赋能千行百业。坚持服务实体经济，发展低门槛智能体开发部署工具，合作研发面向真实作业场景、创造实际价值的智能体，推动智能体嵌入现有生产系统和业务流程，打造标杆型应用。不断降低智能体落地应用成本，助力行业提质增效。 第八条 推动智能体技术普惠共享。共促基础共性技术开源开放，参与国际标准研发与规则构建，通过联合研发、人才培训等，打造全球开发者受益的创新网络。不断提升技术获取和本地化部署便利性，让智能体服务惠及更多国家和地区的用户。 来源： 中国信通院CAICT 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 中金AI十年展望：Personal Agent——消费级AI的破晓时分
articles.summary: 摘要 Personal Agent有望降低通用Agent的使用门槛，释放普通消费者的潜在自动化需求。 我们认为Personal Agent核心能力包括长期记忆、主动服务、安全可控和可靠交付。随着主动需求发现、长期任务管理能力不断完善，消费者能够将更多事务交由Agent处理，推动AI使用人群、人均任务量及后台计算需求持续增长。 我们测算得到：在基准情形下，人均消耗约3.6亿Token/月，硬件成本约23美元/月。 我们将Personal Agent带来的硬件需求分为云端沙箱需求（CPU、DRAM）、推理需求（GPU）和长期记忆需求（SSD）。我们认为，目前部分套餐订阅费或难以覆盖硬件成本，更大的收入空间或来自于抽佣及广告收入。 生态与模型共同构建Personal Agent差异化。 1）生态：平台型助手具有流量入口、丰富商业资源和工具，在获客、服务执行等方面具优势；独立助手擅长跨生态整合。2）模型：自有模型厂商能够开展针对性训练，将真实任务反馈用于模型迭代；独立厂商可以灵活选择模型，通过框架与上下文设计改善产品能力。 2030年中国Personal Agent市场规模有望超过5,100亿元。 我们认为有望形成以下三类商业模式：1） 订阅收入： 通过可量化的任务价值与持续可靠的日常服务，建立分层付费体系；2） 广告收入： 依托用户注意力与需求识别能力，在信息获取及决策过程中提供广告推荐，承接商家营销预算；3） 交易佣金： Agent通过促成订单与完成交易，按一定比例收取佣金。基础情景下，我们测算2030年中国Personal Agent的订阅收入、交易抽佣收入和广告收入空间有望分别达到838、3,918和386亿元。 正文 什么是Personal Agent？ Muse的快速增长为Personal Agent打开消费级AI需求空间提供了早期观察窗口。 Meta于2026年9月8日在美国推出Muse，据Sensor Tower，其上线22天内美国下载量超过500万，并围绕购物、出行、日程管理等场景展开产品探索。Muse呈现出Personal Agent的重要特征：将对用户的长期理解与任务的持续执行相结合，使用户能够将需要完成的事项交由AI处理，减少反复交代背景、协调操作及跟进进度的投入，体现出AI持续参与个人事务的应用潜力。对比海外各大Personal Agent的产品功能、生态、收费模式，我们认为，Personal Agent有望帮助普通消费者将模糊的生活目标转化为可执行的委托，推动AI使用人群及人均任务量进一步扩展。 Muse有哪些特质 Muse在持续执行、长期记忆、授权控制、服务场景上具有独特亮点。 Meta于2026年9月8日在美国推出Muse，由Muse Spark模型驱动，用户可通过App、网页及WhatsApp交代任务。Muse提供了多种功能，以满足用户不同层级的需要：Chat用于持续沟通，Goals组织长期目标及执行计划，Library保存资料与成果；Ideas结合对话、日历和连接账户提出可委托的任务，Feed按用户设定的主题提供信息。Artifacts可以把结果呈现为行程、文档或持续更新的仪表盘。我们认为，持续执行、长期记忆、授权控制和服务场景是Muse区别于传统Agent产品的重要能力 图表1：Muse持续服务场景扩大 资料来源：Meta，中金公司研究部 Personal Agent vs 工作场景Agent 我们认为Personal Agent是能够长期了解用户、主动发现需求，并在授权范围内自主处理和持续跟进个人事务的通用智能体。 Agent能够长期积累个人信息，结合用户偏好和历史行为理解需求，并主动提出建议或执行任务。对于需要长期跟进的事项，Agent可以保留任务状态，在预定时间或相关事件发生时重新开展推理和执行，无需用户持续发出指令。涉及支付、信息发送等关键操作时，用户则通过明确授权保留控制权。我们将其核心能力概括为：长期记忆、主动服务、安全可控和可靠交付。 图表2：海外Personal Agent情况概览 资料来源：各公司官网，中金公司研究部 Personal Agent降低通用Agent的使用门槛，未来有望向更广泛的消费人群渗透。 购物、日程管理等需求普遍存在于消费者的日常生活，但相关操作往往分散于多个应用，需要用户自行搜集信息、协调安排并完成执行。用户只需提出希望达成的结果，Personal Agent即可自主规划并推进任务。便捷的交互方式有望吸引大量用户采用。 主动发现需求与持续推进长期目标有望释放普通消费者的潜在自动化需求，提高用户的使用深度。 专业用户通常具有明确的工作目标，而普通消费者的生活事务更加分散，许多潜在需求需要结合个人信息与实际情境才能被识别。Meta在Muse早期测试中发现，用户面对Agent丰富的功能时往往不知道从何开始，因此专门设计了根据个人目标和历史信息主动提出建议的Ideas功能，帮助用户发现需求并转化为具体任务。同时，长期目标的持续推进也将产生新的自动化工作量。用户只需提出总体目标，Agent便可根据后续信息变化持续识别和执行新任务。我们认为，随着主动需求发现和长期任务管理能力不断完善，普通消费者能够将更多日常事务交由Agent处理，推动人均任务量及后台计算需求持续增长。 硬件需求：Personal Agent对硬件需求的定量测算 由于Personal Agent具备主动服务的功能，每位用户需要有一台云端的“虚拟电脑”，即基于CPU和DRAM资源的沙箱；而Personal Agent在持续推理过程中会产生GPU的推理需求。此外，Personal Agent需要储存用户的个人记忆及文件。 因此我们将Personal Agent对于硬件的需求分为云端沙箱需求（主要是CPU、DRAM）、推理需求（主要是GPU）和长期记忆需求（SSD）。 持久性云端环境带来的云端沙箱需求 在Personal Agent场景下，每位用户的运行环境实际部署在云端容器中，需要占用云端的CPU、DRAM及SSD资源。如何测算沙箱部分的云资源需求量？ 我们认为Agent服务方将以大批量租赁沙箱资源、再分配给用户的方式实现这部分硬件租赁，因此我们先测算1亿DAU场景下所需的硬件租赁成本，再分摊到单一用户（具体假设、测算过程及测算结果详见完整报告）： 图表3：单用户CPU沙箱成本的计算过程 注：价格来源截至2026年11月2日，部分价格来自第三方数据库Holori、Economize，规格实例参考AWS官网一致。 资料来源：AWS官网，Holori，Economize，Muse官网，中金公司研究部 沙箱运行也伴随着SSD的存储需求，用于存储用户的历史记忆文件及各类运行中产生的资料数据。我们假设中度使用的基准情形下，初始需要10GB SSD容量，每月增加2GB。其中冷存储比例约85%。考虑到SSD需求会随着用户使用时长增加而增长，我们在此仅对第一年所需的成本进行测算，实际上SSD成本会随着年份而不断增长。此外，考虑到重度用户数据规模更大，我们假设越是重度的用户，冷存储的比例会更高。 图表4：单用户SSD成本的计算过程 注：价格来源来自AWS官网，截至2026年11月2日。 资料来源：Amazon官网，中金公司研究部 Instinct可以通过电话和消息办理账单、购物、预约及旅行[1]；Manus旗下Cue提供独立个人Agent应用，每个Agent拥有邮箱、电话、钱包和电脑，并支持多个Agent协作[2]。独立助手缺少具备足够流量的获客入口，需要通过明确成果建立用户的首次信任；同时其服务和工具调用受平台授权限制，外部模型、账户连接、电话与浏览器执行等也会产生持续的服务费用，抬升其服务成本。我们认为，独立助手应优先聚焦高频、价值明确的具体场景，通过提高任务完成率、减少用户操作和降低单次任务成本，促成用户持续使用，并逐步积累服务经验与信任。其长期竞争力取决于这些积累能否形成持续的交付优势：即使平台推出同类功能，独立助手仍能更可靠、更省心或以更低成本完成任务，从而留住用户并获得持续付费。 独立助手的优势在于跨生态整合和利益对齐。 1）跨生态整合：用户的信息、工作与消费需求分散在不同平台，独立助手可以围绕用户目标，灵活组合不同厂商的模型、应用与服务，串联信息获取、方案比较和任务执行。比如，客户需求来自微信，资料放在Google Drive，分析在Excel中完成，最后通过邮件交付。独立助手有机会成为这些工具之间的协调者。它的价值取决于能否把整件事办完，而不必要求用户先统一软件体系。同时，平台型助手与其他平台可能存在利益上的冲突，进而导致其权限受限，例如，亚马逊在9月份封禁了Muse代用户在亚马逊网站购物的访问权限[3]。我们认为，独立型个人助手可以凭借其相对中立的身份，在不同生态间选择合适的产品与工具，为用户提供更好的服务。2）利益对齐：独立助手在利益上与用户有更好的一致性，没有偏向特定平台的倾向，可以以相对中立的立场比较服务、推荐方案，逐步建立用户信任，而平台型助手可能更倾向于在自己的生态内完成服务闭环。 articles.title: 民主党大胜，AI数据中心的输家叙事里藏着谁的机会？
articles.summary: 美国中期选举结果让AI数据中心再次站到政策争议的风口。居民电价、电网扩容和社区反对，可能使新建项目面临更严格的审批。但当公共电网越来越难以满足数据中心建设需求，企业自行解决电力供应的意愿也会增强。即使数据中心建设总量放缓，自备电渗透率仍有机会提高，现场发电设备与既有电力接入资产可能迎来新的价值重估。 一、发生了什么？——民主党大胜，AI数据中心为何突然成为输家？ 1. 一场选举，改变了市场对AI基础设施的预期： 美国2026年中期选举出现了超出此前预期的民主党胜利。美联社已报道民主党赢得众议院和参议院控制权；在得州，民主党候选人Gina Hinojosa击败Greg Abbott，当选州长。这一结果尤其值得关注：得州长期是数据中心、比特币矿场和大型能源项目的重要聚集地，而Hinojosa竞选期间明确反对能源消耗巨大的数据中心，并提出暂停新建项目、等待州议会建立新的保护机制。 市场担忧由此集中到一个问题：未来数据中心项目是否会面临更严格的选址、环保、用水和电力接入审查？地方审批趋严可能拉长建设周期，也可能让部分项目重新评估选址和供电方案。但需要区分，联邦国会控制权变化并不等于全国立即实施数据中心禁令；真正决定项目进度的，往往是州政府、地方政府、公用事业监管机构和具体许可程序。 ……

articles.title: 快手孵化的凌川科技完成10亿元B轮融资，下一代芯片瞄准AI视频生成
articles.summary: 11月4日，北京凌川科技有限公司（以下简称：凌川科技）宣布完成10亿元B轮融资。 本轮由亦庄国投屹唐盛和基金、启明创投、朝晖资本联合领投，国泰海通开元、华控投资、国寿长三角科创基金、北工投资、建信（北京）投资等机构参与，石溪资本、龙芯创投、安徽文旅投等产业投资方进入，老股东顺禧基金、水木投资集团、九智资本继续追加。 公司未披露估值，本轮融资将主要用于下一代芯片研发与量产，以及全球市场拓展。 凌川科技前身为快手集团异构计算与芯片事业部，该部门成立于2018年。2024年3月，北京市人工智能基金与快手集团共同发起设立凌川科技，公司开始独立运营。 凌川科技创始人兼CEO刘凌志曾任快手集团副总裁，核心团队来自快手、华为、英特尔等公司。 今年6月，公司宣布完成数亿元A+轮融资，由啟赋资本领投，百度风投、朝晖资本等机构参与，资金主要用于下一代芯片研发、SL200量产扩产及海外市场拓展。两轮融资间隔不足半年。 凌川科技已量产的主要产品是智能视频芯片SL200。据公司披露，该芯片累计销售近10万颗，已应用于快手、阿里云、百度云、哔哩哔哩等企业的业务场景，覆盖快手99.7%的直播转码业务。 今年以来，SL200还通过与电信等合作伙伴拓展至数据中心、智慧安防等应用场景，相关部署规模未披露。 在视频转码之外，凌川科技正将研发重点延伸至AI视频生成推理。据公司披露，其采用3D堆叠技术的下一代芯片已于今年4月流片，近期回片，计划2027年实现规模出货。 公司称，该产品采用自研的延迟确定性DiPU计算架构，并通过混合键合及先进封装技术实现不同功能和制程芯片的异构集成。软件层面，公司围绕DiPU架构开发统一计算平台LUCAS，称已完成对通义万相、Hunyuan Video等视频生成模型的适配优化。 视频生成模型的商业化应用对推理成本、生成速度和硬件利用率提出更高要求。针对特定工作负载设计专用芯片，是降低推理成本的一种技术路径，实际经济性仍取决于模型适配、硬件性能及规模部署效果。 对凌川科技而言，快手提供了早期大规模应用场景。SL200近10万颗的累计销量在今年6月已获披露，11月融资报道仍采用这一数字，尚未明确新的统计截止时点。快手以外客户的采购规模及收入贡献尚未拆分披露，外部市场拓展成效仍有待验证。 与此同时，下一代3D芯片尚未规模出货。芯片回片后的性能验证、量产良率和客户导入情况，仍需观察。专用计算架构还需要软件生态配合，模型持续迭代也将考验芯片及软件栈的适配能力。 后续值得关注的是，下一代芯片的实际出货规模、快手以外客户的收入贡献，以及专用架构能否在真实业务场景中形成可量化的推理成本优势。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 民主党在美国中期选举中实现历史性横扫，不仅夺回国会众参两院控制权，更在得克萨斯、南卡罗来纳、堪萨斯等传统共和党票仓实现意外翻转。这一结果重塑了市场对美国财政路径、AI监管前景与利率走势的预期，全球资产价格随之剧烈重定价。 全球市场经历了典型的"利空出尽"行情。纳斯达克100指数期货一度跌超2%，标普500期货跌逾1%，VIX恐慌指数期货冲破20关口；随后多空易位，美股期货逐步收窄跌幅，韩国综合股价指数由跌4%转为翻涨，黄金重上4000美元关口，白银同步走强，美债全线上涨。 反转背后的核心逻辑在于特朗普的否决权。 民主党掌控国会两院，意味着其财政扩张与减税议程受阻，联邦借贷压力下降，利好美债；但特朗普仍握有总统否决权，市场随即意识到民主党推动立法的空间同样有限，实质上形成政策僵局，恐慌情绪由此平抑。正如Stifel首席华盛顿政策策略师Brian Gardner此前在研究报告中所指出的："市场的本能反应逆转， 因为投资者会意识到，无论哪种情形，政策僵局都是最可能的结果 。" 意外程度超预期，市场第一反应是抛售 选前，预测平台Kalshi已将民主党夺回众议院的概率定价至约99%，参议院的概率亦接近100%，民主党横扫合约价格升至77%。高盛在选举日早间报告中明确指出，众议院结果已被市场消化，参议院走向才是产生意外的主要来源。 然而，最终结果的超预期之处不在于众议院，而在于参议院的翻转幅度与州级选举的全面突破。 民主党在得克萨斯州、南卡罗来纳州、堪萨斯州、爱荷华州等此前被视为共和党防守阵地的选区相继胜出。高盛政治经济学家Alec Phillips此前曾警告，共和党倾向较强的州，共和党候选人历史上最终表现平均比民调高出约3个百分点，实际结果显示这一"民调缓冲"本次并未兑现。 市场的第一反应是抛售风险资产。标普500期货跌约0.9%，纳斯达克100指数期货跌2%，彭博美元现货指数跌0.4%，日元兑美元升0.5%，瑞郎涨幅居G10货币之首，达0.7%。亚洲股市全面下挫，日经225指数一度跌超4%，韩国综合股价指数跌幅一度扩大至4%。 否决权逻辑发酵，抛盘迅速消化 随着市场消化分权格局的实际含义，初期恐慌逐步退潮。核心在于： 民主党控制国会可以阻碍特朗普的立法议程，但同样无法主动推行自身政策——特朗普的否决权构成双向制衡。 Invesco Asset Management全球市场策略师Tomo Kinoshita在据彭博的评论中表示，民主党横扫引发的AI监管担忧"看起来有些过度反应。即便下届国会通过收紧AI监管的法案，特朗普总统仍可行使否决权。" J.P. Morgan Asset Management亚太区首席市场策略师Tai Hui亦指出，特朗普仍掌握贸易与关税、外交政策以及现行监管框架等核心政策工具，分权政府对其实际施政能力的影响有限。Monex Group专家总监Jesper Koll更直言：" 这本质上是一个依赖行政命令运作的强总统制。国会变色，但特朗普的施政风格不会改变。 " 这一逻辑判断推动韩国综合股价指数由跌转涨，日经225指数与中国台湾加权指数亦显著收窄跌幅，美股期货跌幅逐步缩减。 美债走强，财政紧缩预期重新定价 分权政府对美国国债构成直接利好。市场逻辑清晰： 民主党控制国会将压缩特朗普扩大赤字的立法空间，联邦借贷压力下降，对当前规模约40万亿美元的美国国债而言是明确正面信号。 美债收益率曲线全面下行。五年期国债收益率一度跌9个基点至4.68%，十年期收益率下行7个基点至4.89%，随后均有所收窄。 Wellington Management投资组合经理Brij Khurana据彭博表示："分权政府意味着近年来高水平的财政支出将受到约束。从历史规律来看，分权政府格局对美债通常相当有利。"野村证券驻悉尼高级利率策略师Andrew Ticehurst亦指出，蓝色浪潮情景"普遍被认为对美元偏空、对美债偏多，亚洲盘早盘的市场走势与此判断一致。" 不过，瑞穗银行策略师Evelyne Gomez-Liechti此前曾提醒， 不应过度追逐"僵局等于财政紧缩"的叙事——特朗普擅于谈判妥协，国防支出上升与医疗削减计划被稀释的可能性并存，实际财政轨迹或变化有限。 AI与科技股：监管阴影笼罩，但过度反应嫌疑未消 科技与AI板块是本次选举冲击中承压最为集中的领域。民主党横扫引发市场对数据中心建设审批趋严、AI监管立法推进的担忧，叠加此前数周AI基础设施支出回报争议持续发酵，纳斯达克跌幅居主要指数之首。 亚洲科技股受到明显波及。韩国三星电子与SK Hynix各跌约1%，Longbow Asset Management首席执行官Jake Dollarhide据路透表示，民主党横扫"可能给科技板块带来压力，并对AI相关领域形成监管约束，可能放缓我们日常视为理所当然的野蛮增长速度。" Saxo首席投资策略师Charu Chanana亦指出，纳斯达克期货跌幅更深，"反映市场担忧政治权力转移将带来对AI与大型科技公司更严格的监管审视，而当前投资者已对高估值和不断攀升的AI支出持疑问态度。" 然而，多位策略师对恐慌程度提出质疑。Jesper Koll明确表示 ，AI的负面势头"与共和党是否保住多数席位无关"，对AI的批评与担忧"已远超政治层面"。 State Street Global Advisors首席投资策略师Michael Arone据路透直言："我认为市场面临的真正风险不是蓝色浪潮本身，而是投资者对蓝色浪潮的过度反应。" 黄金走强，清洁能源逆势大涨 在股市和科技板块承压的同时，黄金与清洁能源板块呈现出截然不同的走势。 黄金价格上涨逾2%，重上4000美元关口。美元走软与美债收益率下行为金价提供了双重支撑，市场同时押注分权政府将压缩特朗普财政扩张空间，从而缓解通胀预期与财政赤字风险。 清洁能源板块则成为本次选举行情中最大的结构性受益者。 市场押注民主党控制国会将阻止或部分逆转特朗普针对清洁能源项目的系列措施。 韩国Hanwha Solutions盘中一度涨逾22%，HD Hyundai Energy Solutions与OCI Holdings各涨逾12%。美股方面，据Blue Ocean另类交易系统，Enphase Energy与SolarEdge Technologies各涨约12%，First Solar与Sunrun分别上涨11%与8.7%。 市场能否就此出清，取决于后续变量 此番"先崩后拉"行情的背后，是市场在快速完成政治格局重定价后的理性回归。高盛在选举日早间报告中所提出的核心问题——选举能否成为"出清事件并推动股市更广泛的风险重建"——在短期内得到了部分肯定的答案。 Edward Jones高级策略师Angelo Kourkafas据MarketWatch表示， 选举驱动的市场波动历史上持续时间有限，AI主题走向与地缘政治动态才是驱动市场走向年末的核心变量。 Natixis首席美国经济学家Christopher Hodge亦指出，选举结果的直接经济影响"实际上并不大"，更值得关注的是特朗普在中期选举后可能寻求"改变叙事"的政策操作空间。 后续市场的关键观察点包括：美国财政部季度国债发行计划对收益率曲线的影响、AI数据中心建设在各州层面实际推进节奏的变化，以及特朗普政府在分权格局下能否通过行政手段维系其核心政策议程。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 20%涨停！光伏、电池爆发！美国中期选举引发异动
articles.summary: 午后，与新能源相关的光伏、太阳能及电池板块大幅拉升。逆变器中的首航新能午后开盘直线拉升至涨停，锂电板块中的紫竹高科午后亦是转为强势，并封死涨停。正泰电源、上能电气、阳光电源、固德威、昱能科技、艾罗能源等跟涨。 那么，究竟发生了什么？ 据央视新闻报道， 美东时间11月4日凌晨1时，美国中期选举现场投票基本结束，各州将继续统计并公布计票结果。据决策台数据预测，民主党将获参议院100席中的52席、夺回参议院控制权，并预计夺回众议院控制权，将重新掌控国会。美国总统特朗普祝贺民主党并愿合作，但表示可能行使否决权迫使跨党派协议；参议院民主党领袖舒默称民主党人赢得参议院。目前结果均为测算，尚未正式确定，各州认证时间多在11月中下旬至12月。 分析人士认为，股市异动可能与美国中期大选有关。市场可能预期，民主党上台对于新能源产业存在正面驱动。 对行业更重要的变化，是政策不确定性下降、项目审批环境改善，以及未来能源投资预期发生变化。民主党获胜之后，更可能出现的是，阻止部分新能源政策进一步收缩；加强对行政部门能源政策的监督；通过预算、立法和人事安排影响能源政策；为2028年总统大选后的新能源政策转向做准备。 由此，民主党可能推动恢复对太阳能发电项目的政策支持；加强对联邦政府暂停、延迟光伏项目审批的调查；增加对输电网络、电网改造和新能源并网的支持；限制行政部门通过行政命令削弱新能源产业的政策空间。 分析认为，最为直接的影响是，美国新能源产业的中长期政策预期可能改善。储能、电网和光储一体化的重要性可能进一步提升。新能源投资逻辑可能从单一发电设备转向整个电力系统。但企业是否都会受益，还值得观察。 本文来源： 券商中国 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 诺和诺德Q3销售额、利润双超预期，全年增长指引上调 | 财报见闻
articles.summary: 诺和诺德（Novo Nordisk）第三季度业绩全面超出市场预期，并随即上调全年业绩指引，显示这家丹麦制药巨头在经历动荡一年后正重新积聚增长动能。 公司11月4日公布的财报显示， 第三季度调整后销售额达792亿丹麦克朗，高于市场预期的735.5亿克朗；调整后息税前利润为317.2亿克朗，同样大幅超出预期的287.1亿克朗。 受此提振， 公司将全年调整后销售额及运营利润增长预期双双上调至按固定汇率计算的-2%至+2%区间，优于此前8月所定的-6%至持平区间。 公司CEO Mike Doustdar表示，三季度业绩好于预期，肥胖症业务组合表现尤为突出。 此次业绩的核心亮点在于Wegovy口服版的放量。今年早些时候推出的这款减重药片三季度销售额达53.9亿克朗，远超分析师预期的46.4亿克朗。与此同时，可注射版Wegovy销售额为204亿克朗，明星糖尿病药物Ozempic销售额达297亿克朗，均超出市场预期。上述超预期表现有效缓解了市场对诺和诺德能否应对竞争压力的担忧。 三季度业绩全面跑赢预期 第三季度，诺和诺德调整后销售额按固定汇率计算同比增长4%，主要受美国及国际市场GLP-1药物销量持续增长推动，尤以肥胖症领域为甚。调整后息税前利润按固定汇率计算增长27%，增速显著，部分原因在于2025年三季度曾计提约90亿克朗的全公司转型费用，构成较低比较基数。 值得注意的是，报告口径（非调整）的营业利润按固定汇率计算下滑9%，原因是本季度计提了87亿克朗的非现金减值损失，其中包括与ziltivekimab相关的46亿克朗减值，以及因优化生产网络规模产生的41亿克朗减值。 前三季度累计来看，报告口径净销售额为2545亿克朗，同比增长11%；调整后净销售额为2277亿克朗，同比增长2%。 Wegovy口服版成为新增长引擎 Wegovy口服版是本季度最受市场关注的产品。截至三季度末，该产品已在美国、阿联酋、英国及德国完成上市，此后又相继进入四个新市场，目前已覆盖八个国家。 诺和诺德同时披露， Ozempic口服版已于今年5月在美国上市，每周新品牌处方量（NBRx）较上市前的Rybelsus品牌水平增长约100%。 公司表示，Ozempic 2.0 mg剂量版本及Wegovy 7.2 mg单剂量注射笔也正在国际市场加速铺开。 Wegovy品牌在美国新患者启动量方面仍保持领先，在品牌化肥胖症市场的份额超过50%。 管线进展支撑长期预期 在研产品线方面，诺和诺德本季度亦有多项进展披露。在肥胖症领域，联合疗法CagriSema（1.0/1.0 mg）在REDEFINE 9试验第68周显示体重减少21%；口服zenagamtide的AMAZE 9三期临床试验已于9月启动。 在糖尿病领域，CagriSema在REIMAGINE 5试验中显示，在合并肥胖症的2型糖尿病成人患者中，第60周体重减少达12.4%，优于tirzepatide 5 mg的9.1%，同时HbA1c降幅不劣于对照组。 在血液及内分泌疾病领域，Frehemgo（denecimig）已于9月17日获得欧盟人用医药品委员会（CHMP）正面意见，计划于年底前后在欧洲首批上市；美国监管审查仍在进行中，若获批，预计于2027年上半年在美上市。公司还表示，CagriSema正准备于2027年初在美国上市，但仍有待监管批准。 竞争格局仍是核心变量 尽管此次财报数据全面超预期，外部竞争格局依然是投资者的核心关注点。诺和诺德是GLP-1减重药的开创者，当前约有10%的美国人正在使用该类药物。然而，竞争对手礼来（Eli Lilly）凭借其自身GLP-1产品，在美国这一最大单一市场已实现超越。与此同时，多家制药公司亦在积极布局这一高利润赛道。 市场目前聚焦的另一关键议题，是两家公司下一代减重产品能否有效应对肥胖相关并发症，包括心脏病、肾病、睡眠呼吸暂停及关节炎等，这将在很大程度上决定各方市场份额的未来走向。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
